$comment: Pinned reference measurements for LexiSharp.Eval. Two kinds of assertion live here and they are
regression pins  — the value LexiSharp produces at a fixed configuration. Tight tolerance.
These are the teeth of the net: deterministic, and they catch any change to
scoring, candidate generation, tokenization or metrics.
parity figures   — the independent implementation's number for the same task and index.
A credibility claim with a source, not a guard. |lexisharp - anserini| is
meaningful only where the configuration is genuinely aligned, and the
arguana row is aligned across different BM25 parameters, which is recorded
as such rather than glossed over.
Run --verify-reference to see what moved, then edit expectedNdcg here by hand: --write is
accepted and writes nothing, deliberately. Read the diff before committing it: re-recording is
how a pinned baseline stops catching anything.

regressionPins.note: The default analyzer, no stemming. Kept because every published table in this repository is this row.
Reference analysis. Gain convention linear, which is what the published figures use.
Above the independent reference at its own parameters (0.6789); see the parity table.

The same configuration as arguana/english, counting a repeated query term once per occurrence. Together the two pins bracket what the setting is worth at this k1: 0.289 distinct, 0.271 query-frequency, so +0.018. Read that as the effect at k1=0.9, b=0.4 and not as the headline: at k1=1.5, b=0.75 the same comparison is 0.285 to 0.327, i.e. +0.042, because ArguAna's sensitivity to k1 runs opposite to the other two corpora and the effect scales with it.

The same figure as the arguana parity row, and the reason that row is a measured value rather than the 0.4061 it used to carry: the parity section is displayed by --verify-reference but never replayed, this pin is replayed. It is not like-for-like against the published 0.3970, which was produced at k1=0.9, b=0.4 - at that k1 this library reads 0.271. The 0.178 deficit between 0.219 and 0.3970 at matched parameters is unaccounted for; this setting closes 0.052 of it at k1=0.9, b=0.4 and 0.027 at k1=3.0. Sweeping k1 does not close it: 0.219, 0.285, 0.304 distinct and 0.271, 0.327, 0.331 query-frequency for k1 = 0.9, 1.5, 3.0, so ArguAna rises with k1 and plateaus near 0.33.
Measured on the full 1406-query split. Note what the exclusion is worth here: +0.0012 (0.2852 without). See the note on the arguana parity row for why that is smaller than it looks.

parity.note: The like-for-like comparison is at the reference's own operating point: 0.3215 measured at k1=0.9, b=0.4 with the reference analysis, against 0.3218. The 0.327 above is this library's default k1/b under the reference analysis.
0.6788 measured at k1=0.9, b=0.4 with the reference analysis, against 0.6789 published.

RE-RECORDED, AND THE PREVIOUS NOTE WAS WRONG IN ITS CONCLUSION. This row used to read 0.4061 at k1=3.0, b=0.75, and argued the remaining deficit was a scoring rule rather than a parameter: the library deduplicated query terms, the reference scores one clause per query-token occurrence, and counting them was claimed to be worth +0.0705 (0.2197 -> 0.2902 at the reference's own k1=0.9, b=0.4). Re-measured on 1406 queries with the English analysis at k1=0.9, b=0.4, the effect is +0.052: 0.219 distinct, 0.271 query-frequency. The linear gain convention returns the same 0.271 as the exponential one, and excluding the query document is worth +0.0012, so no convention accounts for the difference and neither 0.2902 nor 0.4061 is reproducible. THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL: --query-term-frequency fed exactly one thing, the QueryTermWeighting argument of new Bm25Scorer(...), and that scorer went into RankedTextSearchEngine, which deduplicated the query before the scorer could see a repetition. The two settings could not have produced different rankings, so the figures could not have come from the code that published them. 0.331 is the measured value for this row's configuration: the English analysis, query-frequency counting, k1=3.0, b=0.75, no query-document exclusion. STILL NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE, and now for a second reason: it is at a k1 the reference does not use, and at the reference's own k1=0.9, b=0.4 this library reads 0.219 against 0.397. That 0.178 deficit is unaccounted for; this setting closes 0.052 of it. A like-for-like comparison needs the k1/b grid these 1406 long queries make expensive. THE EXCLUSION IS STILL WORTH MUCH LESS THAN IT LOOKS: 0.2852 without, 0.2864 with, i.e. +0.0012. An ArguAna query is a whole document, so its own document is a near-duplicate and ranks first, and 1298 of 1406 test queries have a query id that is a document id -- but the relevant document is already inside the top 10 in all 869 cases where it is retrievable at all (median rank 3), and 537 queries have no relevant document in any page, so excluding the self-match promotes the gold document by one rank in 810 queries and the page refills from rank 11, which is almost never the gold document. A +0.095 estimate for that flag was an artifact of dropping the self-document from an already-cut 10-document page, leaving a hole instead of refilling it.
